idea-plugin.name: FactoryLine AI Proof
idea-plugin.description:
Your IDE feels slow. Your AI code looks fine. Check both with evidence before you spend another hour guessing.

FactoryLine AI Proof is free, local IDE Guardian + AI proof for JetBrains. Record a short local health window, review what was observed, inspect an AI or teammate diff, and choose the next safe human review step—without uploading source or changing IDE settings.

New in 0.8.19 — SaaS Reality: inspect whether OAuth/OIDC identity, tenant authorization, checkout, webhook, entitlement, feature access, and revocation agree across Clerk, Auth0, Okta, Entra, Cognito, Supabase, Firebase, or another standards-compliant provider. The native status action and Graph Ops view read hash-verified local receipts; they never contact a provider, access credentials, change billing, grant access, deploy, or approve a release.

In 60 seconds: inspect an outcome, fuzzy PRD, or risky diff; challenge whether a test can actually reject the failure it claims to cover; then see the current proof gap before a human decides what may be applied.

Start now: open Tools | FactoryLine | Run First Proof, confirm the workspace, then inspect the local result. Generate an MVP when you need one; a starter is never called production-ready before relevant evidence exists.

What this solves

  • Passing tests that prove nothing: expose missing or stale proof before it turns into a confident-looking review green light.
  • A clear PRD heading toward the wrong build: Intake Grill records a named, byte-bound intent, framework choice, acceptance evidence, and external-effects posture before a mission can require it.
  • AI retries that repeat a failed idea: Proof-Delta requires a changed candidate and fresh hash-bound evidence, or makes the no-gain halt visible instead of consuming another retry.
  • Agent trust that quietly ratchets upward: Earned Autonomy derives an expiry-bound local evidence tier and automatically demotes severe hollow-test or scope-escape findings; it never authenticates an agent or grants permission.
  • Unclear AI or teammate diffs: review the exact local scope, see the declared proof gap, and follow one fact-derived next action.
  • Several tasks in one working tree: review the full diff or focus only the active file, instead of mixing unrelated local changes.
  • AI repair scope can drift or overreach: seal one native Change List, validate only a candidate patch that stays inside it, and keep independent verification plus final IDE apply under human control.
  • Large or remote workspaces feel opaque: measure local workspace shape and path-only WSL/remote context, then review generated/dependency directory signals without FactoryLine touching indexes, heap, caches, inspections, or remote settings.
  • The IDE slows down and guesses start replacing facts: record a short local window of aggregate heap, process CPU when available, indexing state, and EDT dispatch delay; compare a structural continuity baseline before deciding whether a project-model change deserves re-analysis.
  • Lost review context: save a hash-bound local JSON, Markdown, and Mermaid handoff packet that another developer can inspect.
  • Automation without control: every command needs confirmation; FactoryLine does not edit, commit, publish, deploy, upload source, or make a release decision.
  • Several plausible repairs: ProofSearch rejects failed proofs, surviving mutants, scope escapes, test weakening, and error suppression, then explains the smallest verified winner in the Graph Ops Counterfactual Arena.

Start here

  1. Open Tools | FactoryLine | Run First Proof.
  2. Confirm the current workspace.
  3. Review the local setup result in the FactoryLine tool window.
  4. Run factory mvp "Build an approval tracker" --root ., then open Graph Ops to inspect the next evidence step.

Know what is safe to ship

  • Check changed code: see which proof is invalidated by your current diff.
  • Review the exact local scope: inspect the full current diff or just the active file in a dedicated Proof Review tab, with declared findings and one fact-derived next action.
  • Keep AI suggestions and proof distinct: use the optional GitHub Proof Review workflow beside CodeRabbit or another reviewer for one neutral, commit-bound evidence walkthrough. It does not need a vendor account, ingest AI comments, approve, or merge.
  • Keep an agent inside agreed scope: run the local factory plan verify CLI contract to compare a named human-approved plan with the exact diff and surface Proof Debt. It records obligations; it does not execute tests, approve, merge, or change IDE settings.
  • Make UI design reviewable: add the optional Prestige Design Review for a purpose-led brief and visible checks for hierarchy, responsive behavior, affordances, consistency, and declared design tokens. Its findings inform review; they do not certify accessibility, conversion, or production readiness.
  • Leave a durable local handoff: save the hash-bound review as JSON, Markdown, and Mermaid for a teammate or a later supervised repair attempt.
  • Use AI repair without losing team control: turn a selected Change List into a Scope Passport, bind a textual candidate patch to it, and make the separate verifier and human apply steps explicit.
  • Investigate workspace load safely: use Workspace Advisor for a bounded local measurement and manual review paths; it is not an IDE performance diagnosis and never mutates configuration.
  • Verify receipts: inspect local evidence before a release decision.
  • Measure real savings: compare paired time, token, and cost data without inferred values.
  • Run supervised workflows: assemble features, continue from safe boundaries, inspect durable mission graphs, and route secret-free BYOK policies.
  • Follow the exact evidence path: Unified Graph Ops visualizes local requirements, slices, missions, approvals, completions, proofs, verifier sessions, gates, traces, and artifacts without executing them.
  • Compare repairs without trusting another opinion: inspect every hash-bound candidate, exact rejection reason, mutation result, risk, changed scope, proof runtime, and measured-or-unavailable savings. Apply, merge, publish, and deploy remain locked.
  • Keep generation and grading separate: factory verifier binds independent worker and verifier evidence, immutable checks, and hard budgets. It validates receipts; an external supervised runner must enforce runtime isolation.
  • Clarify a PRD before the build compounds ambiguity: run factory prd grill PRD.md --root . for a capped, source-bound question sheet with answer stubs. It never rewrites the PRD or authorizes implementation.

Use FactoryLine when you want to

  • Turn an outcome into a buildable starting point: create a contained MVP from a plain-language goal, then extend it in your normal IDE workflow.
  • Review AI or teammate changes with evidence: connect requirements, tests, policies, and receipts before deciding what is ready to ship.
  • Recover the next safe step after a change: identify proof that can be reused, proof invalidated by a diff, and the fact-derived action to take next.
  • Make team automation inspectable: run supervised, local-first workflows and record paired time, token, and cost observations only when they are measured.

Local by design

The plugin asks before running a command. It does not upload project files or receipts, store API keys, sign artifacts, or decide whether a release is ready.

Works with IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider, CLion, GoLand, RustRover, and DataGrip from the 2025.2 platform baseline.

Availability

FactoryLine's local proof core is free and open source. Optional paid features are not active in this Marketplace build: there is no checkout, entitlement, source upload, credential storage, signing authority, or automatic release authority.

Read the documentation, inspect the source, and review the license terms.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Add SaaS Reality: one provider-neutral, hash-verified local status for OAuth/OIDC identity, tenant/role authorization, checkout, webhook, entitlement, access, and revocation. Unknowns block green; the plugin never contacts or mutates a provider.
  • Add declared Change Profiles to Engineering Judgment: selected Change Lists can expose a named new change kind, deterministic Senior Attention route, and review-due or successor drift. FactoryLine never infers source semantics or approves a change.
  • Add Guardian Core as the first tool-window tab: it summarizes a bounded, local, in-memory IDE-health sample window and exposes navigation-only review routes. Guardian does not diagnose a cause, rank plugins, change IDE settings, or apply a repair.
  • Add IDE Health Flight Recorder and Index Continuity Guard: bounded in-memory aggregate runtime samples plus explicit local structural baseline/compare evidence. Both are observation-only; neither changes IDE settings, caches, indexes, plugins, project files, or remote state, and neither claims a causal diagnosis or duration prediction.
  • Add Intent Ledger: make the selected native Change List's behavioral promise, non-goal, and negative case visible before code review; surface scope escape, stale proof, and coverage gaps using existing local evidence. Capture is named, exact-confirmed local metadata only; inspection never edits source, changes VCS state, runs a test, starts an agent, or declares production readiness.
  • Add Intake Grill, Proof-Delta, Gauntlet Survival Cards, and Earned Autonomy: bind intent before a mission, prevent evidence-free retry loops, make declared negative checks visible, and keep agent trust expiry-bound. These remain local supervision artifacts; they do not run an agent, authorize a repair, or certify production readiness.
  • Add refreshable local Assembly activity and a read-only Developer Memory Brief in the shared Studio and Graph Ops view: exact-diff next-proof actions, redacted Continuity facts, and observed local Git contribution context, without execution, repair, approval, identity, billing, or productivity authority.
  • Add Graph Forensics: sealed semantic lineage, first-divergence and causal-path analysis, deterministic stale-read/write, parallel-write, and duplicate-side-effect findings, plus a non-executing recovery preview.
  • Add ProofSearch and the Graph Ops Counterfactual Arena: compare 2 through 12 hash-bound repair candidates, reject hollow or unsafe candidates, show every loss reason, and select one deterministic verified winner without applying it.
  • Add full Graph Ops review controls for copying verification commands, exporting the displayed decision, validating winner guardrails, and visibly retaining apply, merge, publication, deployment, credential, and connector authority.
  • Add JetBrains Proof Review: review the full local diff or active file with structured, attention-first evidence, safe changed-file navigation, and an explicit local JSON/Markdown/Mermaid handoff packet.
  • Add Verified Repair Sandbox: select one native Change List, create a hash-bound Scope Passport, and reject textual candidate patches that cross its paths. Candidate generation, independent verification, and IDE patch application remain explicit supervised steps.
  • Add Workspace Load Advisor + Remote/WSL Preflight: bounded local filesystem measurements, generated/dependency directory signals, path-only context, and optional local JSON/Markdown/Mermaid reports without IDE or remote mutation.
  • Add the Verifier Plane: hash-bound worker and independent-verifier receipts, deterministic no-progress review, and a visible Graph Ops verifier lane.
  • Add a concise use-case guide for MVP creation, evidence review, safe proof reuse, and supervised team automation.
  • Add Unified Graph Ops: a local, read-only visual map with one fact-derived next action.
  • Add PRD Grill: a deterministic, source-bound question frontier before PRD optimization, compilation, or scaffolding.
  • Add optional GitHub Proof Review delivery: a neutral, commit-bound local evidence walkthrough that can coexist with CodeRabbit or another AI reviewer without importing vendor credentials or comments as proof.
  • Add Plan-to-Proof Review: a strict, human-approved agent-plan envelope, exact diff alignment, named deep-review routing, and explicit Proof Debt through the local CLI and PR evidence surface.
  • Clarify the optional Prestige Design Review lane for UI-scoped work and its review-only boundary.
  • Add Run First Proof for a zero-configuration local setup check.
  • Clarify the Marketplace name, preview, getting-started flow, and privacy boundary.
  • Keep the stable plugin ID and verified compatibility across eight JetBrains IDEs.
